actions.reason: BasicTokenizer._train_str no longer walks each occurrence of the merged pair in Python. It now runs str.replace first. chr(idx) is a new code point, so s.split(chr(idx)) gives the text between merged occurrences. The last char of each nonempty piece is the left neighbour of the next occurrence, and the first char is the right neighbour of the previous one. An empty inner piece marks two adjacent occurrences. Those neighbours are counted in C with _count_elements over itemgetter maps, and the stats updates are applied per distinct neighbour, so the counts come out the same as before. RegexTokenizer.train now reuses the shared pop_top_pairs instead of its own duplicate heap-pop code. pop_top_pairs no longer re-files zero counts, which is equivalent for the basic paths because they delete zero entries, and the regex path keeps max()'s own error when it runs out of pairs. The body of Tokenizer.load moved into the encoding-only module, so training no longer compiles it at import. Outputs are identical and all tests pass: train_ir ratio 0.9530, encode_ir ratio 0.9992.

journal.text:
I worked on train_ir in minbpe. My first passes trimmed regex.py and base.py: I collapsed the regex train loop and dropped dead code at the end of base.py. I also tried moving helpers into _slow.py and _heap.py. Then I rewrote BasicTokenizer._train_str in basic.py. It now runs str.replace and then splits on chr(idx), so it gets neighbour counts from the edges of each piece instead of walking every occurrence in Python.

The first evaluation was rejected with train_ir ratio 0.9956 against the required 0.9900. The third was rejected at 0.9993. The fifth was accepted, with train_ir going from 336885755 to 321045086, a ratio of 0.9530. encode_ir came in at 0.9992 and outputs were identical. I submitted that 170-line candidate. It is queued for replay.

I now think the regex and base cleanups barely move instruction counts. Real gains come from pushing per-occurrence work into C string methods.

Next I would apply the same replace and split idea to encode in base.py and regex.py to target encode_ir.
